.qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r5/rules/projects/webdev-task-template (tests/scored/polish/judge.toml incl. template responsive_layout row, tests/app_context.md, instruction.md, folder layout)
evidence: Requirement surface: the product is interactive and time-varying but not responsive or themed. instruction.md:5 asks for other people's moves within fifteen seconds without reload 'and without closing the card I have open, wiping the note I am typing or moving my cursor'. instruction.md:7 asks to keep the reader's place while earlier messages load and while a message arrives, and never to touch the draft or cursor. hireops_rules.md section 5 (lines 117-123) and section 6 cover seen marks, unread counts, scrolled-up arrival, the 30-message paging and drafts across sign-out. instruction.md:11 says 'We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout'. The task correctly drops the template's 390x844 responsive_layout polish row, and visual/prompt.md:14 says 'Assess desktop craft at a conventional desktop viewport. No phone layout or theme switching is required.' No resize or toggle is owed, and none is graded. Every time-varying or interactive promise is driven by actions and waits rather than read from a still first paint. (1) Waits without interaction: functional/prompt.md:47 (protocol V) says 'Without reloading or clicking in this page, wait up to 15 seconds (a wait-for call, or snapshots; accept what is present at the first snapshot at or after 15 seconds)'. functional/prompt.md:41 (protocol U) says 'Every reading in U is made without reloading, navigating or clicking in Rafael's page: wait up to 15 seconds after the other person acts'. polish/prompt.md:14 says 'After that action do not reload, navigate, click or type in the observed page until the update has been seen or 15 seconds have passed. Read document.activeElement, field values and scroll offsets with page.evaluate; reading is not interaction.' Rows hro_live_board, hro_msg_exchange, hro_unread_counts, hro_unread_scrolled_up and hro_seen each say 'without reload' and fail when the change shows only after a reload or click. (2) Preservation under live change is set up by real interaction, then measured. hro_pol_live_board (polish/judge.toml:23) opens the details, clicks the note box, types an unsaved note and scrolls. A separate context makes the move. The row then checks that the details are open, the note text is unchanged, the note is still document.activeElement, scroll is not reset and further typing appends. hro_pol_live_thread (line 32) does the same for the composer at the newest message. It also has a timing positive control: 'If no update arrives within 15 seconds, preservation cannot be shown and this row is 0', so a dead app that never updates cannot earn preservation credit for doing nothing. (3) Scroll mechanics are driven. hro_pol_earlier_place (line 41) takes getBoundingClientRect().top before and after 'bring in earlier messages', and hro_unread_scrolled_up scrolls up, has Noor send and reads place, notice and count. (4) Keyboard, focus and transient UI: hro_msg_compose uses Shift+Enter and Enter, then reads the box and focus. hro_refused_put_back reads document.activeElement after a refused move. hro_pol_failed_send aborts one send via a route or setOffline, then retries. hro_pol_session_resume ends the session in a second tab and presses Enter in the first. hro_drafts switches views and reloads. Gates are correctly limited to sign-in, create and independent-context readback. Weak-app probes: an app that pauses polling while a field has focus misses the 15-second arrival in hro_pol_live_board and scores 0. An app that re-renders the board and drops the open card or note fails the same row. An app that only refreshes on reload fails hro_live_board, hro_msg_exchange, hro_unread_counts and hro_seen. A conversation that jumps to the bottom on arrival fails hro_unread_scrolled_up. Conforming alternatives such as SSE, polling of 15 seconds or less, sockets, a drawer or modal card view, and any route or label layout are all accepted: the prompts discover controls by intent, and app_context.md:33-34 says 'never assume the reference implementation's routes'. Golden runtime evidence (scripted, not judge): I verified the SHA256 of workspace.cjs (749036d0...) and results/workspace.json (1c7e6fcc...) against raw-evidence-index.json. I also verified board.js, threads.js and app.js against the frozen bytes (a177dc0c..., a013ecaa..., 6ce330f3...). workspace.json group 13 'live board: another person's move arrives without reload; open card, note draft and focus kept' passed with arrival_ms 802. Group 14 (arrival while reading keeps draft, focus and scroll, not marked read until viewed; earlier-load keeps place within 2px, workspace.cjs:323-344) passed. Groups 15 and 17 passed, and page_errors is []. Residual risk, so risk=true: (a) No configured claude-code/GLM judge trajectory exists. The raw-evidence-index scope says 'Full configured grading/workload ... are absent', so it is unmeasured whether the judge actually observes the no-click 15-second waits and preservation checks as written, and whether those waits fit inside functional timeout 9000 and polish 900. (b) The scripted golden never checks the board-scroll-not-reset clause of hro_pol_live_board (workspace.cjs:296-313 checks the note, focus and open details only), so that one golden clause is unmeasured, although board.js updates the DOM in place by key and is unlikely to reset scroll. (c) Minor, P3 only: a card-details design that replaces the whole board view could not show the other card's move 'on this page' and would score 0 in hro_pol_live_board. However, instruction.md:5 ('show up on my board ... without closing the card I have open') reasonably implies the card stays open with the board visible, so this is not a hidden requirement. On design alone this row is a Pass. The missing measurements above cannot be waived.
